Filtered Relevant Items:
1. [9] ZooKeeper logs “Connection request from old client … will be dropped if server is in r-o mode” when a client omits the optional read-only flag; the discussion proposes lowering this message from WARN to DEBUG.
2. [10] The same warning is described as acceptable for older clients lacking the read-only flag; updating the client to send the flag avoids it.
3. [15] A matching ZooKeeper warning was explicitly judged not to be a problem by itself; the actual connection issue in that case was an incorrect Kafka port.
4. [20] A 10-second ZooKeeper session expired after an approximately 10.6-second JVM/host pause, causing an HBase region server to abort after receiving the expiration event.
5. [18] A discussion states that session expiration and end-of-stream messages can reflect a client crash or stall rather than a ZooKeeper server failure.

External Knowledge Summary:
- The “old client” warning indicates omission of the optional read-only capability flag and is generally not evidence of a failed connection unless the server is in read-only mode [9][10][15].
- ZooKeeper sessions with 10-second timeouts can expire when client processing or the host pauses for longer than the timeout, including during long JVM/GC pauses [20].
- Repeated expiration or disconnect events may therefore point to stalled, paused, or terminated clients rather than a ZooKeeper server-side exception [18][20].
